meta.name: us-retirement-limits
meta.title: US retirement contribution limits, RMD Uniform Lifetime Table, and IRA-eligible metal rules
meta.disclaimer: This dataset restates publicly available U.S. tax-administration figures for research and software use. It is not legal, tax, or investment advice, is not an official IRS or Treasury publication, and may lag later corrections or legislation. Confirm every figure against the cited primary source before relying on it. Contribution limits can also be reduced by taxable compensation, income phase-outs, plan terms, and aggregation rules that are not fully encoded here.

The deductible amount and Roth eligibility can be reduced by compensation and AGI phase-out rules that are not encoded in this row. The age-50 IRA catch-up became subject to an annual COLA under the SECURE 2.0 Act and increased to $1,100 for 2026 (IR-2025-111; Notice 2025-67).

sources.label: TSP Historical information on contribution limits

employer_plan_limits.notes: The IRC § 402(g) elective-deferral limit is a personal, aggregated limit across 401(k), 403(b), governmental 457(b), and TSP employee deferrals. Agency/employer automatic and matching contributions do not count toward 402(g) but do count toward the § 415(c) annual-additions limit. Catch-up amounts under § 414(v) are in addition to the 402(g) limit and are not annual additions.

rmd_uniform_lifetime.used_when: Lifetime required minimum distributions for an employee or IRA owner when the surviving spouse is not the sole designated beneficiary, or is the sole designated beneficiary but is not more than 10 years younger. statute.rule: The acquisition by an IRA of a 'collectible' is treated as a distribution equal to the cost of that collectible. 'Collectible' includes any metal or gem and any stamp or coin, with the exceptions in § 408(m)(3).

named_coin_exceptions.description: A gold coin described in paragraph (7), (8), (9), or (10) of 31 U.S.C. § 5112(a)
A silver coin described in 31 U.S.C. § 5112(e)
A platinum coin described in 31 U.S.C. § 5112(k)
A coin issued under the laws of any State

statute.bullion_exception: Gold, silver, platinum, or palladium bullion of a fineness equal to or exceeding the minimum fineness that a contract market (as described in section 5 of the Commodity Exchange Act, 7 U.S.C. § 7) requires for metals which may be delivered in satisfaction of a regulated futures contract, if such bullion is in the physical possession of a trustee described in 26 U.S.C. § 408(a).
statute.notes: The statute incorporates contract-market delivery fineness by reference; those exchange rules can change. Coins that are not in the named U.S. Mint / state-issue list (for example many foreign bullion coins, or U.S. coins described in other paragraphs of 31 U.S.C. § 5112) are not automatically excepted as coins. They are excepted only if they meet the bullion fineness test and are held by the IRA trustee. This file does not determine whether any particular product is IRA-eligible.
